title: Minimum-Cost Assay Design on Named Latent Roots for Causal Identification

proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved the labeled certificate reduction, shared-cost query-menu equivalence, and measured-law recovery under its stated graphical and positivity conditions. The three cited hardness and ID sources were independently checked and attested; both specialist referees passed. D0.5 still graded the delivered paper incremental because semantic completeness, an augmented proof-producing compiler with solver integration, and comparative practical evidence remain outside this proposal.
tldr: A deterministic finite compiler sends a catalogue of exact observational assays on named shared latent roots to standard minimum-cost identification design with exactly one permitted action per root. The source class is one finite-state recursive SCM in which the named set \(L\) exhausts every latent common cause of \(O\), its declared child sets supply every shared incidence, all remaining exogenous disturbances are variable-specific and independent, and every \(P_{O,M}\) is a compatible marginal of that same SCM. Relative to Akbari et al. (2023), the theorem compares only with their bidirected-edge-action restriction: the observed DAG \(D\) is fixed, directed-edge uncertainty is excluded, and one pairwise root per removable bidirected edge gives a cost-preserving embedding of that subclass. That pairwise subclass already makes exact assay selection NP-complete and rules out polynomial-time \((1-o(1))\ln |L|\)-approximation unless NP has quasipolynomial-time algorithms. Grouped assays are a strictly different action system because one price can remove every incidence of an arity-at-least-three root and overlapping labels make a shared adjacency survive until all supplying roots are assayed; independently priced edge actions cannot preserve all such action subsets, incidence deletions, and costs. The typed target-copy schema fixes a canonical topological order, every interval endpoint, every top, subdivision, copy, sink, root-action, and connector vertex, all directed and bidirected incidences, exact connector multiplicities, the target and action sets, and exact polynomial vertex and edge counts. The compiler preserves every assay subset, all costs, and root-labeled hedge certificates even when root child sets overlap, ancestral target districts contain several vertices, and several queries share the same paid assay. Each positive-probability measured-root assignment has an explicit CADMG whose fixed-parent and bidirected incidences are derived from the exhaustive source SCM. A successful design yields each causal query solely from \(P_{O,M}\) by conditional ID in these strata and mixing with the intervention-invariant law of \(M\) when the original query metadata remain available. The transformed tuple \((H,T,Z,c),M\) alone omits \(Y_q,x_q\), so only an augmented-input proof-producing compiler remains open.
gap: Akbari et al. (2023), Proposition 4.2, covers an edge-action domain that permits directed-edge uncertainty as well as bidirected-edge uncertainty, whereas the present source problem fixes \(D\) and makes no claim about directed-edge actions. Its bidirected-only restriction embeds cost-preservingly as one pairwise named root per removable edge, but independently priced edge actions do not represent one observational assay that simultaneously removes a whole root clique while preserving incidences supplied by overlapping unassayed roots.
fill: The project defines the exhaustive named-root SCM class, derives every measured-root stratum CADMG from its structural equations, constructs a deterministic grouped-root target-copy graph with a canonical order and complete typed incidence schema, proves forward and reverse labeled hedge maps against that schema, proves the pairwise-root embedding and the grouped-action nonrepresentability boundary, separates shared-root query blocks, transfers family optimization without repeated charges, and recovers root-stratified ID formulas from the compatible marginal \(P_{O,M}\).
